faq.a: Aaiz represents Arabic عائذ (ʿāʾidh), meaning “one who seeks refuge” or “one who takes protection.” The lexical sense does not establish personal-name popularity.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aaiz?
faq.a: The recorded form عائذ is Arabic and is associated with the root ع و ذ (ʿ-w-dh), related to seeking refuge or protection. This identifies the word’s linguistic origin, not regional naming frequency.
Aaiz is a Latin-script spelling used for Arabic عائذ (ʿāʾidh). Transliteration conventions vary, so the Arabic form is more precise than any one Latin spelling.

faq.q: What is the root of Aaiz?
faq.a: The form عائذ is associated with the Arabic root ع و ذ (ʿ-w-dh), related to seeking refuge or protection.

This record does not establish Aaiz as a Qur’anic personal name. Arabic origin and a religiously compatible meaning are not proof of a specific scriptural reference.

faq.q: What does Aaiz mean in Urdu?
